Everyone knows that the S.Ct recently "legalized" gay marriage. What very few people know is how the court reached this decision. Most, actually, don't even care. But the way that the court reached its decision is actually extremely important, and essential to understanding your question.

The Court could have reached its decision employing the principle of "Comity." Comity means that the states have to respect each others laws. When someone with property in several states dies die, for example, they don't need several wills. They only need a single will that meets the minimum requirements of their domicile state. Once this will is probated in their domicile state, it has to be respected as valid by all the other states in which that person had property, even if it fails to meet the other states' probate requirements. This comes form Article 4 Section 2, "The Citizens of each state shall be entitle dot he Privileges and Immunities of Citizens of the Several States."

So the Court could have said "if someone is married in state X, then this marriage is valid in state Y because of states have to respect each others laws."

But they didn't do this. Instead of basing their decision on Art 4 § 2, they based it on the the Due Process Clause of the 14th Amendment(!) "nor shall any State deprive any person of life, liberty, or property, without due process of law."

This is huge, because you probably didn't know that rights protected under the due process clause are very, very strongly protected by the courts. Beginning in the 50's the S.Ct. re-interpreted the Due Process clause to not only strike down all the racist Jim Crow laws in the Deep South, but also seized control of local society:

Schools could not be segregated, so judges decided what kids attended what schools, and forced local school districts to buy buses and hire bus drivers to enforce their decisions. Businesses could no longer discriminate on the basis of race. Private clubs that were not open to the public were fined and disbanded if they didn't permit blacks to join. This was expanded in order to get rid of closet racism. Today, businesses that even have the appearance of discriminating can fined into bankruptcy, which is why they work so hard to make sure that they employ sufficient quotas of each race.

My point is this: protecting homosexual marriage under the Due Process Clause is HUGE! ENORMOUS!
